new_libraries.name: C_Allocator
new_libraries.author: David Lafreniere
new_libraries.sentence: Fixed block memory allocator in C: static pools, no heap, deterministic, with malloc/free style use.
new_libraries.paragraph: fb_allocator hands out fixed-size blocks from a static pool; x_allocator combines several pools into a malloc/free/realloc style API that picks the smallest block that fits. No heap fragmentation, constant-time allocation. Thread-safe on FreeRTOS, ThreadX, Zephyr and CMSIS-RTOS2 with a build option.

new_libraries.name: C_StateMachine
new_libraries.author: David Lafreniere
new_libraries.sentence: Compact table-driven finite state machine in C, with guard, entry and exit actions and typed event data.
new_libraries.paragraph: Define states, events and transitions with macros; the state engine handles internal and external events, guard/entry/exit actions and event data. Event data comes from C_Allocator's fixed block pools, so no heap is used.

new_libraries.name: SimpleSocketProtocol
new_libraries.author: David Lafreniere
new_libraries.sentence: Socket-based binary protocol for UART and other serial links between CPUs, with ACK/NAK, retries and CRC.
new_libraries.paragraph: Simple Socket Protocol (SSP) sends messages between sockets over any byte link: UART, USB serial, SPI. Every message is CRC-checked and ACKed, and resent until the other side ACKs. Portable C with a small hardware/OS layer; also runs on Windows and Linux, so a board can talk to a PC program built from the same code.
